description_en: The Bistabara Śikhara Temple complex consists of three temples that date from approx. 13th to 15th centuries and are located beneath the village of Bistabara. The Bistabara village committee has built a stone and cement wall around the monuments.The monument in the north-westernmost direction of the complex is Bistabara Śikhara Temple 3, which is introduced ehre. The two other temples areJUM0450andJUM0451. The Temple 3 is oriented to the north-east. The door is facing, another smaller temple (JUM0450). The pediment is ornamented, with horizontal friezes carved in stone. The doorjambs and lintel are missing. The ceiling embellished with a flower or star pattern. The sanctum is empty. It could have contained aśivaliṅga. Theśikharais crowned by twoāmalakadiscs of recent origin that have been poorly carved.Suchśikharaswere erected throughout the Karnali Basin from the 13th to the 15th century (Andolfatto 2019). The rarity of inscriptions onśikharatemples (locally calleddeval) complicates the dating of this type of monuments. The pediments of the Bistabara temples have horizontal friezes identical to those found on the twośikharatemples of Tarpibada (JUM0441andJUM0442), 2.5 km to the north. These temples can be dated between the 13th and the 15th century. Furthermore, a stone memorial pillar located 5 meters to the north of the Bistabara temples (JUM0453) bears the date of ŚS 1422 (1500 CE). It is plausible that the pillar and the temples were built around the same time.The local name of the Bistabara temples is Pañcadevala. The term led D. R. Sharma to write that the site originally contained five temples (Sharma 2012: 181-182). This is most unlikely, since "Pañcadevala"is a terminology often used in west Nepal to talk about places with more than oneśikharatemple. Moreover, thepañcadevalaplan is mostly found in the districts of Dailekh, Achham and Kalikot, which correspond to the area controlled by the Rāskoṭi kings. This dynasty ruled between the end of the 14th century and the end of the 18th century (Andolfatto 2022). So far, nopañcadevalais attested in the district of Jumla.
monument_assessment: Good (very few light surface damages, renovated or repaired)
